manifest_name: Stage 1 — Verified African American Public-Art Candidates

candidates.street_address_or_precise_public_locatio: Auburn Avenue NE and Courtland Street NE, Atlanta, GA 30303
candidates.access_notes: The City of Atlanta public-art archive places the bronze/granite work at a public street intersection. Current condition and access were not field-verified in Stage 1.
candidates.work_status: Documented by the City collection as a 1996 installation; no current field condition was collected.
candidates.source_publisher: City of Atlanta Mayor's Office of Cultural Affairs
candidates.artist_evidence_note: The City collection page credits Brian Owens.
candidates.location_evidence_note: The City collection page gives Auburn Avenue NE and Courtland Street NE. Dry-run coordinates were derived from that public intersection, not imagery.
candidates.community_context_evidence_note: The City source describes James Tate as a historic Sweet Auburn community leader and 'the father of black business in Atlanta.' The tag records documented subject/community history, not an inference about Brian Owens.
candidates.source_rights_note: Factual source only. The City page does not grant MWM rights to reuse its photography or other media.
candidates.missing_evidence_reason: The dry-run intersection coordinate is within the near-coordinate threshold of the unrelated 'Open Mic at Café Circa' map entity; resolve the public-art point with an official map or field check, confirm current access/work condition, and obtain owner approval for the metadata/canonical-route work before any import.
candidates.deduplication_note: No normalized-title or exact-address collision was found. The near-coordinate result is not a merge recommendation because the existing entity has a different title and address.

candidates.access_notes: Mural Arts lists this work as On View at the recorded public address.
candidates.work_status: On View, according to Mural Arts Philadelphia; restoration is documented in 2001 and 2008.
candidates.artist_evidence_note: Mural Arts lists Jane Golden and Dietrich L. Adonis in the artist field.
candidates.location_evidence_note: Mural Arts lists 4022 Parkside Avenue and provides the recorded coordinates in its location link.
candidates.community_context_evidence_note: Mural Arts states the mural was commissioned by the National Council of Negro Women and commemorates a celebration of the enduring strengths and traditional values of the African American family.
candidates.source_rights_note: Factual source only. No Mural Arts image or other media may be reused without separate permission or a documented license.
candidates.missing_evidence_reason: A complete Tier 2 record requires an independent Tier 1 or second independent corroborating source for future owner review; the current metadata/route gap also blocks import.

candidates.street_address_or_precise_public_locatio: 300 E. 31st Street, Chicago, IL 60616, within Paul Laurence Dunbar Park
candidates.access_notes: Chicago Park District classifies the work as an outdoor sculpture in a public park. Current condition/access was not field-verified in Stage 1.
candidates.work_status: Documented as commissioned and erected in 2014; no current field condition was collected.
candidates.artist_evidence_note: Chicago Park District credits Debra Hand.
candidates.location_evidence_note: Chicago Park District gives the street address and identifies Dunbar Park. Dry-run coordinates are derived from the source-supplied public address.
candidates.community_context_evidence_note: Chicago Park District says the monument honors 'one of the most significant figures in African American history' and describes Dunbar as among the nation's first African American poets to receive national attention.
candidates.source_rights_note: Factual source only. Chicago Park District imagery and other media are not licensed to MWM by this manifest.
candidates.missing_evidence_reason: No critical source-field gap found, but current access/work condition must be confirmed and the owner-approved public-art metadata/canonical-route work is required before any import.
